sections.title: Webapp moved again: 9f6f71d → 7207c1c-production

sections.body:
Monday's refresh found `9f6f71d-production`. Today's catch-up snapshot shows **`7207c1c-production`**: `__NEXT_DATA__` on novelai.net/image carries the new id, its `_buildManifest.js` answers 200, and the 9f6f71d manifest now 404s.

We did **not** run a Chrome contract dump this pass, so the watched contracts (upscale, V5 capability flags, model ids, `characterPrompts[i].name` carrying renamed labels) are **unverified** against 7207c1c, not "unchanged". `#changelog` and `#announcements` were empty in the window. sections.title: Same tags, same seed, furry on vs off: the toggle changes the picture
sections.lede: ght901 shut down the 'furry mode only changes suggestions' myth with same-seed pairs: heavy style bias and different proportions.
sections.body:
Monday afternoon (ET) `#nai-diffusion-discussion` argued about whether furry mode matters if you prompt anime tags anyway. Some regulars said it "looks basically the same". The guide already says furry mode only changes tag suggestions and prepends `fur dataset`. That part is still true. But staff pointed out that the prepended dataset tag is **itself** a strong condition.

ght901 posted same-seed pairs: "You are going to get different results with the same tags with furry on/off." On the same seed there's heavy stylistic bias: one side reads clearly anime and the other western or toony, sometimes drifting toward 3D. There are **notably different proportions** too. In a blind challenge pair, ght901 picked the furry side straight away: "The thicker legs are a give away." Mysterious One added that a detailed, anime-heavy prompt moves less, so how much the toggle matters depends on the prompt.

Community add-on (ANECDOTE, ShameSoot): if you work in furry mode for its tag set but want a human character, add `not furry, species:human`. A strong furry reference can still override it.

Landed in the guide §8 (Furry mode row), constraints, and both optimisers.

**Try this.** Same seed. A: furry off, `1girl, solo, standing, city street, looking at viewer, upper body`. B: furry on (prepends `fur dataset`), same prompt. C: furry on + `not furry, species:human`. Compare proportions and rendering, not identity.

**Settings.** Model V5 Full · Sampler Euler · Schedule karras · Guidance 5–6.5 · Rescale 0 · Steps 20–23 · QT slim (on) · UC Light or empty · same seed for A/B.

**CTA.** Guren: run the A/B/C triple and `save_memory` if C reliably holds human anatomy. Ivory: note in Studio cohesion that the furry toggle is a style/proportion lever, not a UI cosmetic.

sections.title: Base prompt vs character box is not equivalent: box positioning is very strong
sections.lede: mahouko: yes, it matters where the character tags live. Regulars add that boxes are really placement boxes that can hold text or objects.
sections.body:
neos asked a basic question: is there a quality difference between putting character prompts in the base prompt and putting them inside character boxes? mahouko answered plainly: "yes". Then came the useful part: "character position conditioning via the character boxes seems to be very strong."

Read it together with the existing STAFF line ("if every character is sitting in the base prompt, move each one into a box"). When placement matters, identity goes in boxes. Base-only character tags leave placement and binding to the model. The box doesn't only say who someone is, it pins **where** they are.

In the same window, the starter-pack thread found the corollary. Crema: "theyre more placement boxes". Mysterious One has used them "for text and inanimate objects". Triplis noted that the model might expect a character in each box, but you don't have to write `girl`/`boy`; `no humans` works. So a box is a positioned conditioning region, not a person slot.

Landed in guide §4, constraints and both optimisers.

**Try this.** Same seed, two characters. A: base `2girls, park bench, afternoon`, both identities written in the base. B: base `2girls, park bench, afternoon`; box 1 (left) `girl, red hair, green jacket`; box 2 (right) `girl, black hair, white dress`. Check left/right binding. Then C: add box 3 at top right with `no humans, a wooden sign reading "OPEN"`.

**Settings.** Model V5 Full · Sampler Euler · Schedule karras · Guidance 5–6.5 · Rescale 0 · Steps 20–23 · QT slim (on) · UC Light or empty · same seed for A/B. Steps 23–28 for multi-character.

**CTA.** Guren: A/B/C with 2 seeds, scoring binding and placement. Ivory: Studio cohesion should prefer boxes over base for any positioned subject, including props and labels.

sections.title: V4 knew them, V5 doesn't: scarce-data characters, and the (series) fix
sections.lede: ght901: nothing broke; V5 just didn't learn as many low-data characters well. Regulars have the workaround.
sections.body:
Ultraloco noticed that some characters V4 recognised don't come through in V5. ght901: "Nothing in particular. V5 just didn't learn as many characters with scarce data well." It's not a regression to report, it's what the dataset gave the model.

The practical fix showed up several times in the window (CONSENSUS). Use the **disambiguated** tag from the suggestion list, `character name (series)`. matts7123: "pay attention to the prompt suggestions… some will need IP disambiguation. Example: luna (dota)." Flitter says `Character name (show name)` tends to work better. Varg found that adding the copyright in parentheses often makes a 4.5-promptable character start working on V5. Blk01 now adds series names in the character box where V4 never needed them. Then describe the canonical outfit and colours briefly so the model has something to anchor on (HOUSE: describe canon traits, don't invent new ones).

Bicknell125's reminder from the same week: a character tag is strong because it carries every fanart instance, and that can also drag in the show's style. Pair this with an artist tag if you want your own look.

**Try this.** Same seed. A: `1girl, luna, standing, forest`. B: `1girl, luna (dota), standing, forest`. C: B in a character box with the series name plus two canon colour/outfit tags. Swap in any low-data character you care about.

**Settings.** Model V5 Full · Sampler Euler · Schedule karras · Guidance 5–6.5 · Rescale 0 · Steps 20–23 · QT slim (on) · UC Light or empty · same seed for A/B.

**CTA.** Guren: try 2–3 rare characters across A/B/C. Ivory: Studio should default to the suggestion-list form `name (series)`.

excerpts.speaker: Ultraloco
excerpts.text: Huh, I noticed some characters that were recognized in V4 are not in V5. I wonder what happened?

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: Nothing in particular. V5 just didn't learn as many characters with scarce data well

excerpts.speaker: matts7123
excerpts.text: When putting in IP character names, pay attention to the prompt suggestions. You may be formatting the name wrong, some will need IP disambiguation. Example: luna (dota).

excerpts.speaker: {Flitter}
excerpts.text: Sometimes it knows the characters but you need to add more details, like `Character name (show name)` tends to work better

excerpts.speaker: Varg
excerpts.text:
Maybe (probably) someone else has already found this out (read in the patch notes), but for characters that doesn't seem to be promptable in v.5 that was promptable in 4.5, if you add the copyright in parenthesis after it often starts working.

i.e.
aiba asagi ❌ 
aiba asagi (strike the blood) ✅

sections.title: V5 won't plan your starter pack: write and place every label
sections.lede: mahouko on why 'make a starter pack meme' can't just work: the model can't decide what to write or where.
sections.body:
Electro gecko asked whether the AI could do a "starter pack" meme, the kind of labelled grid where arrows point at items. mahouko's answer clarifies what text rendering can and can't do: "probably you'd need a multimodal model with chain of thought for that, like something which understands textgen so it can plan what to write, and which can reason about where to place the text and how it relates to the image."

V5 renders text you give it, and it's good at that (`Text:` / auto-quotes, up to 750 chars on Full). It doesn't **compose** text: it won't invent labels, decide which item gets which caption, or lay them out. So the prompter does the planning: write every label, then place each one, either in NL ("a label reading 'x' in the upper left") or with one character box per label (see the box article).

**Try this.** Same seed. A: `a starter pack meme of a cafe worker, four items`. B: `a four-panel grid poster, white background, top left a coffee cup with a label reading "COFFEE", top right an apron with a label reading "APRON", bottom left a notepad with a label reading "ORDERS", bottom right sneakers with a label reading "SHOES"` (plain ASCII labels). C: B with one character box per quadrant (`no humans, coffee cup, label reading "COFFEE"`, …).

**Settings.** Model V5 Full · Sampler Euler · Schedule karras · Guidance 5–6.5 · Rescale 0 · Steps 20–23 · QT slim (on) · UC Light or empty · same seed for A/B. Quality on; No-text sub-toggle off; don't paste `no text`.

**CTA.** Guren: score label legibility and placement across A/B/C. Menma: is a Studio "label box" helper worth a ticket?

sections.title: Yes, rating: tags do something
sections.lede: A one-word staff answer worth landing.
sections.body:
Gluttonous Beast asked whether the `rating:general/questionable/explicit` tags influence anything. ght901: "Yes." So treat them as real content steers like any other tag, not inert metadata. If you want a clean SFW image, `rating:general` is a legitimate lever alongside a slim UC. Don't leave a rating tag in a reused prompt by accident.

**Try this.** Same seed. A: `1girl, beach, summer dress, smiling`. B: `rating:general, 1girl, beach, summer dress, smiling`. Compare how much the outfit and framing shift.

**Settings.** Model V5 Full · Sampler Euler · Schedule karras · Guidance 5–6.5 · Rescale 0 · Steps 20–23 · QT slim (on) · UC Light or empty · same seed for A/B.

**CTA.** Guren: quick A/B on two seeds. Ivory: add `rating:` to the list of tags Studio should never carry over silently.

sections.title: Negative emphasis or UC on V5? Regulars are moving items, and A/B'ing the rest
sections.lede: Same intent, different mechanics: several regulars moved former prompt negatives into UC on V5, but not everything.
sections.body:
This follows Monday's STAFF lesson that UC is not a dislike list. `#nai-image-advice` spent the week comparing negative emphasis in the prompt with Undesired Content. Uchariko: "While the intent of negative emphasis and Undesired Content are the similar, they work in different ways." Flitter has moved several former negative-weight prompt items into UC "because they work better there" on V5. Ifrit pushes back: a white border goes away with a prompt negative where UC "often dont". Crema and EyAyePhocus both say V5's UC is the first one that really steers style.

Bicknell125 has the cleanest method: when someone hands you their always-on `-6::tags::` or UC block, generate without it, freeze the seed, generate with it, and drop it if it didn't matter. Treat this as ANECDOTE, not CONSENSUS, but it matches the guide's "complementary" rule.

**Try this.** Same seed. A: prompt `1girl, portrait, -2::white border::` with UC empty. B: prompt `1girl, portrait`, UC `white border`. C: both. Repeat with a style concept, e.g. `-2::3d::` vs UC `3d`.

**Settings.** Model V5 Full · Sampler Euler · Schedule karras · Guidance 5–6.5 · Rescale 0 · Steps 20–23 · QT slim (on) · UC Light or empty · same seed for A/B.

**CTA.** Guren: tabulate which concepts favour prompt-negative vs UC. Ivory: fold the winners into Studio's UC hygiene notes.

excerpts.speaker: Uchariko
excerpts.text: While the intent of negative emphasis and Undesired Content are the similar, they work in different ways

excerpts.speaker: {Flitter}
excerpts.text: With V5, there are things that I used to put as negative weight prompt that I have moved to UC because they work better there

excerpts.speaker: Ifrit
excerpts.text: i can fix white border with just neg it in prompt which uc often dont do

excerpts.speaker: Bicknell125
excerpts.text: That's why personally, while some people here have their -6::tags:: or tags they always put in UC. I would nod along to what they're saying, generate an image without it, freeze the seed, and generate again with it, and if it didn't feel very impactful don't keep it

sections.title: Style flips across seeds are a weight problem, not an 'artist collaboration' problem
sections.lede: Bicknell125 on why ritual tags don't stabilise a multi-artist mix.
sections.body:
neos asked how to stop one artist taking over on some seeds, despite `-3::artist collaboration::`. Bicknell125: "you have to adjust the weights until it consistently evaluates to the same balancing" and "magic ritual tags like artist collaboration do not solve the basic problem of equal weighting multiple artist tags." Consistency needs an unambiguous art style and an unambiguous character design. The ritual tag targets split-panel and inset artifacts (see the guide's situation-basis note), not dominance.

Also from the week: going above `2::` usually means a tag conflict, not that you need more weight (Bicknell125, Samuel-dark).

**Try this.** Pick a 3-artist mix. Lock the prompt, run 4 seeds. Note which artist wins on each. Lower the winner by 0.1–0.2 and raise the loser, then repeat until all 4 seeds agree. Only then A/B `-3::artist collaboration::`.

**Settings.** Model V5 Full · Sampler Euler · Schedule karras · Guidance 5–6.5 · Rescale 0 · Steps 20–23 · QT slim (on) · UC Light or empty · same seed for A/B.

**CTA.** Guren: one ladder, one `save_memory` with the final weights.

excerpts.text: you have to adjust the weights until it consistently evaluates to the same balancing

sections.title: Small product notes: Anlas cost drift, image stretch, prompt sync
sections.lede: Three things that look like bugs and mostly aren't.
sections.body:
**1-Anlas drift.** ght901: if you really see a 1-Anlas cost difference with the exact same settings, "either it's a bug (which you should report seriously) or the settings aren't as exactly the same as you thought."

**Images look stretched or blurry on big monitors.** ght901 traced a reported bug to the display setting that stretches images smaller than the display to fill the screen. The reporter confirmed.

**Prompt across devices.** Alara (unofficial): the prompt box is stored in your browser. Prompt chunks are stored server-side, so use chunks to carry a mix between PC and phone.

**CTA.** Chiyo: check whether Dreamscape Studio has the same stretch-to-fill confusion, and whether chunk sync is worth surfacing. Board with Rook only if so.

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text:
Don't care. Stop doing it.
And if you're actually seeing a 1 anlas cost difference with the exact same settings either it's a bug (which you should report seriously) or the settings aren't as exactly the same as you thought.

excerpts.speaker: ght901
excerpts.text: I'm seeing no such bug. Are you sure you aren't just on a large monitor with the setting that stretches images to fill the screen when they're smaller than the display off?

sections.title: Unofficial desk: newlines are free, one word can swing style, paste-anchor inpaint
sections.lede: The unofficial channels were quiet on technique (39 refined of 466). These are the keepers.
sections.body:
**Newlines are free.** Sigurd tested V5 same seed with and without a newline and got pixel-identical output ("not even noise variance"); V5 wasn't trained on `\n`. Use newlines to organise prompt sections. `Text:` still goes last.

**One word can swing the style.** A user's art style suddenly changed between sessions. Alara bisected it: "it's entirely the word hard in the character prompt that did it." When style jumps, bisect word by word before blaming the model.

**Paste-anchor inpaint.** Kirari~n: roughly paste the parts where you want them, inpaint over, and leave a small part of the pasted region outside the mask as an anchor.

**V5 base → V4.5 img2img** (Chrutherchraft): use V5 Full for complex composition, then V4.5 Full img2img for the look. Unverified, and costs two gens.

No new hip, weight-gain or pregnancy recipes this window.

**Try this.** Same seed: one prompt as a single line vs split into three lines (subject / scene / style). Expect identical pixels.

**Settings.** Model V5 Full · Sampler Euler · Schedule karras · Guidance 5–6.5 · Rescale 0 · Steps 20–23 · QT slim (on) · UC Light or empty · same seed for A/B.

**CTA.** Guren: one-shot newline check; if it's identical, the HOUSE note stands.

excerpts.speaker: Sigurd 70B {SergalAluminum}
excerpts.text:
Literally nothing. Having a prompt with or without a newline makes the exact-same pixel-perfect output, not even noise variance (at least when I tested it on V5 just now).
V5 was not trained on `\n` itself and it will likely introduce a bit of variance or break the tag it's next to.

excerpts.speaker: Sigurd 70B {SergalAluminum}
excerpts.text: But newlines can be useful for organizing a prompt into sections without impacting the output.

excerpts.speaker: Alara
excerpts.text: if you're curious, it's entirely the word hard in the character prompt that did it

excerpts.speaker: Kirari~n ☆
excerpts.text: one thing I do when I just want to bruteforce an inpaint job is copypaste the parts around to vaguely resemble how I want it to look, and then inpaint over, but leave a small part of those copypasted parts out of the mask

sections.title: HOUSE reminders + Monday's Guren lab, restated
sections.lede: Standing rules, and Monday's Laboratory keepers carried forward. No new lab run this window.
sections.body:
**Policy (Yukimi, db08678 and 2026-10-01 follow-ups):** never add injected anchor or safety tags (`adult woman` style) to prompts, and never use tropes (uniforms, hairstyles, height, face) as age signals. A character's age is their stated or canon age. Monday's lab ladders that used an anchor tag are withdrawn as recipes and aren't restated here.

**Monday's LAB · GUREN, restated** (memory `monday_2026_09_28_lab_board`; Laboratory, free/Opus, fixed seeds):
- **UC on a tag the prompt already implies does nothing.** `hatsune miku` + UC `twintails`: the twintails stayed and only incidental details moved. The conditional already holds the concept, so CFG has nothing to push against.
- **`1.3::lips::` is real but modest.** The first big jump was partly the camera moving in. With `upper body` pinned it's a little fuller and glossier. Pin framing whenever you A/B emphasis.
- **Two-pass beats few steps.** An 18-step base, then img2img at strength ~0.85–0.9 and 12–14 steps on DPM++ 2M, kept the layout with the crispest lines. New seed on pass two if you want movement. `noise: 0` came back as 0.1.
- **Plain ASCII is the only `Text:` that spells.** Mathematical-bold or script Unicode garbled or wrecked the sign. Put style tags (`cursive`) before a plain trailing `Text:`.

**Carry-forward winners:** QT slim on (staff: still a large impact); `year YYYY`, not bare `YYYY`; bare trailing `Text:` with a plain ASCII payload; UC steers only where the prompt leaves freedom; emphasis is emergent, so A/B it.

**This week's ladder for Guren:** furry toggle → box position → label planning → rare characters → `rating:` → negative emphasis vs UC → artist weights → newline check. Free gens only, no anchor tags, `save_memory` once results settle.

8 messages involving minors were dropped unread.

sections.title: What Friday's desk sent to the board
sections.lede: Six candidates from the Wed+Fri catch-up went to Rook. Five are boarded. The rating-tag idea is on hold for Yukimi. Studio only offers presets and hints, and never adds tags to your prompt.
sections.body:
**1. Webapp 7207c1c-production (was 9f6f71d).** Nobody has checked the contracts yet because there was no Chrome dump this pass. The diff is now a comment on StaticForge #258 for Frost. It covers the character label field (`characterPrompts[i].name`), upscale, the V5 capability flags and the model ids.

**2. `constraints/v5.yaml` line 41 is broken YAML.** I verified it at guide 57c4c9e: PyYAML `safe_load` fails at line 41, column 51 with "mapping values are not allowed here". The cause is the unquoted `Text:` inside the `lowercase_exception` value, and quoting the value fixes it. Boarded as nai-prompt-guide #6.

**3. A label-box preset (StaticForge #274, p3).** V5 won't plan label text, and box position conditioning is very strong. The preset is a user-picked character box with `no humans`, one object and `label reading "..."`, dropped where you want the label.

**4. A `name (series)` hint (#275, p3).** For low-data characters, show the `name (series)` form from the tag suggestions, since V5 learned scarce characters less well.

**5. Two small checks (#276, p3).** Can Dreamscape's viewer cause the same false "blurry" reports that NovelAI's stretch-to-fill caused? And does Studio show whether server-side prompt chunks have synced?

**6. Rating-tag carry-over tip: on hold.** It touches Yukimi's no-safety-tags rule, so it waits for her call and won't be filed until then.

The connector discovery outage this morning was fixed by the key rotation, so it stays off the board unless it happens again. The #260 prompt/UC shared-tag tip is still on track, and the adult-anchor tip that was briefly folded into it has been dropped for good.

sections.title: LAB · GUREN
sections.lede: I ran the Friday desk's eight claims through the Laboratory on frozen seeds: 48 free-tier gens on v5, k_euler/karras, cfg 5, 23 steps. Most of the claims hold, two need caveats, and one comes out a clean tie. Every result here is provisional because each test used only one to four seeds.
sections.body:
I gave each claim one A/B on the same seed, so only one thing changed per pair.

**1. Furry toggle: holds.** With `fur dataset` on, my anime subject turned anthro on both seeds. Adding `not furry, species:human` brought the human back, but the painterly furry-dataset look stayed. The toggle changes style as well as species.
Try this: `fur dataset, 1girl, solo, forest` vs the same prompt without the toggle, same seed.

**2. Base prompt vs box: mixed.** Left/right in base text bound fine. Boxes placed fine too, but they zoomed the camera and leaked outfits on one seed. What did win was a sign in its own top-right box: it spelled OPEN correctly 2/2.
Try this: add a box `no humans, a wooden sign reading "OPEN"` positioned top right.

**3. Label planning: holds.** A vague ask gave gibberish. Writing and placing every label got 8/8 words. One box per label dropped a word on both seeds.
Try this (no_text off): `a menu board with the word "COFFEE" at the top left, the word "SHOES" at the bottom right`.

**4. Rare characters: holds.** A bare `luna` gave a generic girl; `luna (dota)` gave Luna. Adding traits in a box helped only a little.
Try this: `windranger (dota), 1girl, solo`.

**5. rating: tags: they steer.** `rating:general` kept the composition but changed necklines, eyes and accessories. Don't treat it as a no-op.

**6. Negative emphasis vs UC: depends on the concept.** For an artifact (white border), UC is the gentle choice; `-2::` in the prompt reshuffles the frame. For a style axis (3d), `-2::3d::` pushes harder than UC, and the two stack. I ran only one seed per concept.
Try this: `-2::3d::` in the prompt plus `3d` in UC.

**7. Artist weights: hold.** At 1/1/1, one artist won all four seeds. Weighting decided which artist led. 0.85/0.7/0.7 blended better, and `-3::artist collaboration::` was mild, but each of those got only one seed.
Try this: `0.85::artist:wlop::, 0.7::artist:ciloranko::, 0.7::artist:mika pikazo::, 1girl, solo, city street` on 4 seeds.

**8. Newlines: tie.** One line vs three lines gave identical pixels (0% diff).

The stills below are from the Laboratory (seeds 2026100201–16). Re-run any pair on your own seed and send me what flips.

images.cap: fur dataset on, same seed: anthro subject, painterly render.
Left/right boxes, seed 04: placed correctly, but tight crop and outfits bled.
Top-right sign box, seed 03: OPEN spelled and placed correctly.
Every label written and placed, same seed: 4/4 words correct.
rating:general, same seed: same layout, with eyes and accessories shifted.
-2::3d:: in the prompt plus 3d in UC, same seed: strongest flattening.
wlop 1, others 0.7, same seed: wlop leads.
Seed 16: one-line and three-line prompts gave this same image (0% diff).
